Hmm interesting.

I'm guessing that means that more generally if you set those two parameters to N, then `anchor=oldest` or `anchor=newest` will get you N messages (supposing there are plenty of matching messages), whereas the other three (a date, `first_unread`, or a message ID) will get you 2N + 1 messages.

**Greg Price** · 2026-03-26 00:02 UTC

Definitely in the case of a message ID, the 2N + 1 behavior seems right. There's one message that is the anchor, and then we're returning N messages before it and N messages after, just like the parameter names say.

**Greg Price** · 2026-03-26 00:05 UTC

And then the current behavior is effectively saying that conceptually:
* The `oldest` and `newest` anchors don't refer to any message, but rather to specific points in the history that are beyond all the messages. Seems reasonable, though the opposite would also have been reasonable (referring to the one message that is oldest or newest).
* OTOH the `first_unread` anchor refers to a specific message, namely the first unread message. This also seems reasonable, though the opposite would also have been reasonable (referring to the point just before the first unread message).
* And a date also refers to a specific message. It's not obvious to me which message that would be — is it the first message after the given timestamp, or the last message before it?

**Greg Price** · 2026-03-26 00:10 UTC

So most of those feel quite reasonable to me individually, but a little inconsistent among themselves.

The date behavior is the one that most feels wrong to me in that list. If we're going to have any anchors that refer to an abstract point between/outside the messages, rather than a specific message — as in fact we do, namely `oldest` and `newest` — then a date seems like the prime example of an anchor that should behave that way. That's because there really is canonically referring to a point that can't be expected to have any one message at it; and if it does get resolved to a single message, there's no clear natural answer to which one message that should be.

**Apoorva Pendse** · 2026-03-26 12:41 UTC

The parameter description for the `date` anchor makes it sufficiently clear, IMO.

I felt the opposite and think the `oldest` and `newest` descriptions are misleading and don't quite cover the concept you wrote:

(replying to Greg Price)
> * The `oldest` and `newest` anchors don't refer to any message, but rather to specific points in the history that are beyond all the messages.

For convenience here's the excerpt from /api/get-messages:

> **anchor** string optional [](https://zulip.com/api/get-messages#parameter-anchor) Example: `"43"` Integer message ID to anchor fetching of new messages. Supports special string values for when the client wants the server to compute the anchor to use: * `newest`: The most recent message. * `oldest`: …

I expected all special anchors to compute and return a valid message id after reading this, but only some do.

**Greg Price** · 2026-03-26 18:07 UTC

Yeah, I think it'd be pretty reasonable to have all of the anchors resolve to a specific message (and therefore return N+1 or 2N+1 messages).

**Greg Price** · 2026-03-26 18:07 UTC

And that quote is helpful, thanks. I agree that it looks like we're already clearly saying in the docs that each of the anchors resolves to a specific message, not a point in history beyond or in between the messages, and so should have the N+1/2N+1 behavior.

**Tim Abbott** · 2026-03-26 23:34 UTC

Hmm. I'm not certain this is a case where the implementation details are leaking out, and the result is that the  `oldest`/`newest` behave a bit oddly...

The `N` behavior for those is convenient: A lot of clients want to ask for "50 messages starting with the newest", aka the 50 latest messages, and I suspect it was intentional that we wanted it to be the case that you could put in `50` and get 50 messages back, not 51.

**Tim Abbott** · 2026-03-26 23:35 UTC

Now, I think that mattered a **lot** more before we have `found_newest` and `found_oldest` -- long ago, clients were computing based on whether they got `num_before` items back, and thus the possibility of an off-by-one bug land mine here was a lot more significant.

**Tim Abbott** · 2026-03-26 23:37 UTC

So maybe the actual history here is that we intentionally did this kinda quirky thing several years ago, to avoid a very real class of client confusion/bug... But that our improved protocol no longer binds us to do that, and we have the option to change it. But it would still mean a lot more API requests with non-round numbers of messages returned.

It does seem like `get_openapi_parameters` handles JSON encoded parameters...

```python
def get_openapi_parameters(
    endpoint: str, method: str, include_url_parameters: bool = True
) -> list[Parameter]:
    operation = openapi_spec.openapi()["paths"][endpoint][method.lower()]

**Lauryn Menard** · 2026-03-18 17:21 UTC

**Zixuan James Li** · 2026-03-19 01:28 UTC

This part of `get_openapi_parameters` handles query parameters wrapped in `Json[...]`. An example of such parameters would be [`narrow`](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/f9ca86c246857d37091996ff6de4a0f57892c934/zerver/views/message_fetch.py#L345):
```py
@typed_endpoint
def messages_in_narrow_backend(
    request: HttpRequest,
    user_profile: UserProfile,
    *,
    msg_ids: Json[list[int]],
    narrow: Json[list[NarrowParameter]],
```
Its corresponding schema can be found [at](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/f9ca86c246857d37091996ff6de4a0f57892c934/zerver/openapi/zulip.yaml#L8447-L8449) `operation["parameters"][x]["content"]["application/json"]["schema"]`:
```yaml
      parameters:
        [...]
        - name: narrow
          in: query
          description: |
            [...]
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                items:
```

`JsonBodyPayload` (a.k.a. `Annotated[Json[T], ApiParamConfig(argument_type_is_body=True)]`) implies that `Json[T]` should describe the schema for the entire request body. This is common for webhooks, but unseen for documented endpoints in `zulip.yaml`.

When we expect there to be a request body, I think `get_openapi_parameters `indeed only [handles](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/f9ca86c246857d37091996ff6de4a0f57892c934/zerver/openapi/openapi.py#L382-L384) `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`: 
```py
    if "requestBody" in operation and "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" in (
        content := operation["requestBody"]["content"]
    ):
```


See #**api documentation>OpenAPI requestBody@1622347** for some background on the use of `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (instead of `application/json`).

**Lauryn Menard** · 2026-03-19 16:00 UTC

Thanks @Zixuan James Li for that explanation and conversation link!

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2026-03-23 10:59 UTC

Previous discussion on this: #**api documentation>JSON-encoded data in request body**

**Agnish Bauri** · 2026-07-03 16:16 UTC

Update on this, I dug into `get_openapi_parameters`, curl example generation, the `test_openapi` consistency check, and the API docs argument-table renderer. The fix is narrower than it looked.

`check_openapi_arguments_for_view` needs no changes at all. `JsonBodyPayload` args are already registered under the literal name `"request"` (`typed_endpoint.py`'s `request_var_name`, for any param with `argument_type_is_body=True`), matched by plain set-equality against whatever parameter names come out of the yaml. Type-checking also already collapses any object-typed schema to `dict` regardless of nesting, so `push_requests: list[APNsPushRequest | FCMPushRequest]` doesn't need special handling either.

The actual gap is three places:

1. `get_openapi_parameters` has no branch for `application/json` as a `requestBody` content type - only `x-www-form-urlencoded` and `multipart/form-data`. Planning to add one that emits a single `Parameter(name="request", ...)` (matching the sentinel above), probably with a new `kind="body"` so callers can tell "whole-body JSON blob" apart from a keyed field.
2. `generate_curl_example`/`get_openapi_param_example_value_as_string` assumes every parameter renders as `name=value`. Needs a branch to render the body param as a raw JSON blob instead.
3. `render_parameters` in `zerver/lib/markdown/api_arguments_table_generator.py` builds the "Arguments" table from the same unfiltered `get_openapi_parameters()` output and uses `parameter.name` directly as the displayed argument label. Left alone, that'd show a table row literally labeled "request" which is meaningless to a reader, since it's just our internal matching sentinel. Probably needs a `kind == "body"` special case here too: skip the name-as-argument row and render the schema's own description plus a field breakdown instead (we already have `render_object_details` for rendering an object schema's properties, used elsewhere in this file for nested object parameters).

**Agnish Bauri** · 2026-07-03 16:17 UTC

`tools/test-api`/`test_curl_examples.py` need no changes, they're encoding-agnostic. Bonus: once this is in the spec, the `openapi-core` request validation we already run on every test request stops no-op'ing for this path and starts validating it for real.

Two open questions which can be discussed by maintainers here:
* For the generated curl example: `--json '<blob>'` is the cleanest option - it sets the body and the right `Content-Type`/`Accept` headers in one flag, but it needs curl ≥ 7.82 (March 2022), so it'd break for anyone on an older curl. `-H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '<json>'` is more verbose but works on any curl version. Leaning `--json` since this audience is server operators.
* For the arguments table: is rendering the body's field breakdown (skipping the "request" row entirely) the right call, or is there a preferred way we already document whole-object parameters elsewhere that I should match instead?

The plan will be to send the tooling change as its own PR first (no currently-documented endpoint affected), then follow with the actual `/remotes/push/e2ee/notify` doc.

**Agnish Bauri** · 2026-07-14 12:44 UTC

**Agnish Bauri** · 2026-06-15 08:24 UTC

Bumping this thread up for clarity on questions on this endpoint. I will be opening a new PR for this endpoint, considering last PR got closed.

The schema is done and the OpenAPI argument/response checks are passing.
But when I ran the full suite with it documented, five tests fell over. They sort into two distinct issues, and both come down to a convention call rather than anything wrong with the schema, so I wanted to check
here first.

The root of it is that documenting an endpoint flips on request/response validation for *every* test that touches it, which is where these two surface.

**1. The optional avatar upload turns the request into multipart.** (one test)

`add_bot_backend` will take an avatar through `request.FILES`:

``` python
# zerver/views/users.py
if len(request.FILES) == 1:
    avatar_source = UserProfile.AVATAR_FROM_USER

```

multipart/form-data; boundary=BoUnDaRyStRiNg.
Valid mimetypes: ['application/x-www-form-urlencoded']
```

The only multipart endpoints we have right now (`/user_uploads`, `/realm/emoji/`) are just hard-skipped in `validate_test_request`, so I couldn't find a precedent for an endpoint that's mostly urlencoded but
optionally multipart.

The ways I can see to handle it ->
1. Document the urlencoded params and mark that one success-path test `intentionally_undocumented`.
2. Extend the multipart skip-list to `POST /bots`.
3. Actually document a full `multipart/form-data` variant with the file param.

**Agnish Bauri** · 2026-07-01 18:01 UTC

Update on this. Digging further, the plan I agreed to with @thedance needs correcting on one point, and there's a cleaner fix than I thought for most of it.

**The ORM rework doesn't actually finish the job.** I tested it directly: patching `assert_num_bots_equal` to count via the ORM does stop the GET from tripping `ServerNotFound`, but 3 of the 4 tests then fail one line
later, right at `self.create_bot()`, the bot-creation POST itself. Turns out `Realm.host_for_subdomain()` reads `REALM_HOSTS`/`EXTERNAL_HOST`, and that's also what the test client uses to pick the default `HTTP_HOST` for every request in the test, POST included. So under `REALM_HOSTS={"zulip": "127.0.0.1"}`, the create-bot POST goes to `http://127.0.0.1/json/bots`, gets a 200, and hits the same `ServerNotFound` the GET did. So "creation still goes through `client_post`" is true, but it doesn't actually save us. The POST needs
fixing too, not just the count check.

**Better fix: pin the request host instead of moving to the ORM.** Since `Realm.host` is a pure settings computation, independent of the actual request Host header, I pinned `HTTP_HOST="zulip.testserver"` on the twoshared helpers instead of rerouting through the DB:

``` python
def assert_num_bots_equal(self, count: int) -> None:
    result = self.client_get("/json/bots", HTTP_HOST="zulip.testserver")
    ...

def create_bot(self, **extras: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    ...
    result = self.client_post("/json/bots", bot_info, HTTP_HOST="zulip.testserver")
```

Full `test_bots.py`: 94 tests, down from 5 failures to 2. This keeps full request and response schema validation for these tests (no coverage drop the way moving to ORM would have), and the `REALM_HOSTS` override still
fully drives `get_bot_domain()`, since that's computed from settings, not
from the request's Host header.

**One test is genuinely stuck, and it changes my answer on`skip_openapi_validation`.** `test_add_bot_verify_subdomain_in_email_address` still fails, but differently now: a real 400, "Account is not associatedwith this subdomain." It overrides `EXTERNAL_HOST` itself (not just `REALM_HOSTS`), and `get_subdomain_from_hostname` resolves the request's realm by checking whether the Host ends in `.{EXTERNAL_HOST}`. Any Host I pick either:
- ends in `.testserver`, which matches `servers:`, but no longer matches the overridden `EXTERNAL_HOST`, so the request resolves to the root  domain instead of hamlet's realm, and `validate_account_and_subdomain` correctly (by design) rejects it; or
- ends in `.example.com`, which resolves to the right realm, but isn't in
  the spec's `servers:` list, so it's `ServerNotFound`.

There's no host value that satisfies both at once while `EXTERNAL_HOST` is being overridden, so this isn't fixable by picking a smarter test Host. Since it's down to a single call site now, not four, I think your
`skip_openapi_validation=True` idea is actually the right-sized tool here. I was wrong to write it off earlier as "shared infra, let's not."

**Agnish Bauri** · 2026-07-01 18:02 UTC

One instance on how it'd actually apply: it only helps if this test doesn'tgo through the pinned helpers above. With the host pinned, this test's failure becomes a genuine `validate_account_and_subdomain` rejection
(wrong realm), an application-level 400 that `skip_openapi_validation` has no bearing on, since that check runs before OpenAPI validation ever does. So this one test would need its own local `client_get`/`client_post`
calls, left unpinned so the host resolves naturally to `zulip.example.com` (where the app logic already succeeds, I confirmed this produces a real 200 under the hood, it's purely the schema validator that rejects the host), with `skip_openapi_validation=True` on those specific calls.

So here's the proposed plan: land the `HTTP_HOST` pin for the shared helpers (fixes 3 of 4 outright, no downside), and give `test_add_bot_verify_subdomain_in_email_address` its own unpinned, `skip_openapi_validation=True` calls for the one spot that needs it. Does that work for you, or would you still rather do the general `ServerNotFound` catch in the validator instead?

## documenting /users/me/avatar endpoints

*2026-05-23 to 2026-05-26 · 7 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/412-api-documentation/topic/documenting.20.2Fusers.2Fme.2Favatar.20endpoints/with/2466779)*

**Agnish Bauri** · 2026-05-23 11:05 UTC

While continuing #38510 (avatar API docs), I ran into a server-side issue I'd like a sanity check on before bundling any fix in.
**The issue:** `zulip-api-py`'s `client.call_endpoint(..., files=[fp])` sends the multipart file part without an explicit `Content-Type`. Django parses that as empty string in this case (and other client/server combinations are likely to produce `application/octet-stream`). `set_avatar_backend` then passes `user_file.content_type` straight through to `upload_avatar_image`, which checks it against `THUMBNAIL_ACCEPT_IMAGE_TYPES`, so a valid JPEG uploaded via the Python client is rejected as `BAD_IMAGE: Invalid image format`. The practical consequence is that I can't add a working Python example for the endpoint without a server change.

**What I'm leaning toward:** `upload_avatar_image` already falls back to `guess_type(user_file.name)[0]` when `content_type is None`. My current thinking is to extend that condition to also cover the empty-string and `application/octet-stream` cases:

```python
if not content_type or content_type == "application/octet-stream":
    content_type = guess_type(user_file.name)[0]
```

But I'm not sure that's the shape you'd want, so I wanted to check before pushing. A test having both placeholder content types plus the "no recognizable filename extension" rejection path is straightforward to add either way.
**A few questions:**

1. Does extending the existing fallback feel right, or would you rather see the recovery happen in `set_avatar_backend` (keeping `upload_avatar_image` strict about its contract)? Open to other shapes too.
2. `upload_emoji_image` and the realm icon/logo upload paths almost certainly have the identical issue,  worth covering them in the same PR, or scope this to avatars and follow up separately?
3. Bundle with the API docs PR as a prep commit, or land as its own PR first?

**Alex Vandiver** · 2026-05-23 11:12 UTC

I think it's fine to guess if the content-type is empty, but I would not guess if the client explicitly said it was application/octet-stream.  The client needs a reliable way to say "do not do anything magic on these bytes"

**Chris Bobbe** · 2026-05-25 22:59 UTC

This looks like it might need more comment from the backend folks; @Sahil Batra would you take a look? I'm not really following the backend questions, but of course I'd like more endpoints to be documented. :slight_smile:

**Alex Vandiver** · 2026-05-26 00:21 UTC

This also does not really seem like a *documentation* question -- it seems like a *behaviour* question.

**Sahil Batra** · 2026-05-26 15:13 UTC

I agree with @Alex Vandiver's suggestion to let client pass the correct type and let backend guess the type if it is missing.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2026-05-26 15:18 UTC

**Agnish Bauri** · 2026-05-26 16:32 UTC

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2026-08-25 14:33 UTC

Server registration to bouncer & sending analytics data won't be restricted to provide "mobile push notifications” service only. One can independently register for services like "Security alerts",  "get listed in open communities directory", etc.

**Agnish Bauri** · 2026-08-28 13:39 UTC

While reviewing #39734, @Prakhar Pratyush raised a question which we should settle.

These endpoints' request/response schemas mirror our internal analytics/registration models i.e, `POST /remotes/server/analytics` uploads `RealmCount` / `InstallationCount` / `RealmAuditLog` rows, and I
documented them with those names (both in field descriptions like "the last `RealmCount` analytics row", and, in the follow-up PR, as component schemas named `RealmCountDataForAnalytics` etc.).

The concern is putting internal model names in the public docs couples the docs to those names, so a model rename silently becomes an undocumented API change and nothing guards it. These endpoints' curl examples are in `UNTESTED_GENERATED_CURL_EXAMPLES`, and the request/response validation that does run only checks the wire fields, not these name labels, so a rename wouldn't be caught.

So, what convention do we want?

1. Keep the model-derived names and handle the API change via the changelog.
2. Document everything with API-facing names fully decoupled from Django models.
3. Something in between (e.g. keep the field names, but drop the model names from prose descriptions).

**Lauryn Menard** · 2026-08-28 13:58 UTC

I'd refer to them as "audit logs" generally. And if we need to be more specific in the type of log, then do that via prose vs using the model name.

#39930 has updated the API documentation for the following endpoints:

* [`PATCH /messages/{message_id}`](/api/update-message): Fixed a bug where passing the `stream_id` that the message is already in was processed as a channel move.

**Chris Bobbe** · 2026-08-21 00:49 UTC

A straightforward bugfix; no zulip-flutter issue to file.

**Chris Bobbe** · 2026-08-21 01:00 UTC

For why this announcement failed to post (similar story as #**api documentation>new feature level: 497@2513011**): 

- Looks like the GitHub Action `notify-if-api-docs-changed` is responsible for posting these.
- It's marked as `needs: check-feature-level-updated`.
- But this time, `check-feature-level-updated` failed, because of a dangling `ZF-25c66e` that @Aman (amanagr) fixed in zulip/zulip@cec212c9d, having seen the alert posted by `check-feature-level-updated` at #**automated testing>main failing@2509072**.
- There isn't anything that causes the `notify-if-api-docs-changed` action to re-run after a given failure, so it didn't re-run.

**Chris Bobbe** · 2026-08-21 01:06 UTC

The dangling `ZF-25c66e` was inserted by Claude, following these instructions in .claude/CLAUDE.md:

> […] Document the changes in that file with the header `**Feature level ZF-XXXXXX**` and an unordered list (`*` bullets) of the additions or changes, formatted to match `api_docs/changelog.md`.

That instruction was wrong. A header doesn't belong in the file created by `tools/create-api-changelog`; it's [added automatically](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/996a116a5/zerver/openapi/merge_api_changelogs.py#L89) by `tools/merge-api-changelog`. @Prakhar Pratyush fixed that instruction in #39946.

**Chris Bobbe** · 2026-08-21 21:17 UTC

Sent #40002 to mitigate this (see #**api documentation>new feature level: 497@2513395**).


## new feature level: 510

*2026-09-05 to 2026-09-09 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/412-api-documentation/topic/new.20feature.20level.3A.20510/with/2520113)*

**GitHub Actions** · 2026-09-05 10:21 UTC

#40090 has updated the API documentation for the following endpoints: 

* [`GET /events`](/api/get-events), [`GET /messages`](/api/get-messages), [`GET /messages/{message_id}`](/api/get-message), [`POST /messages/flags`](/api/update-message-flags), [`POST /messages/flags/narrow`](/api/update-message-flags-for-narrow): Added `hide_link_previews` as a supported [message flag](/api/update-message-flags#available-flags) that can be toggled by the user. When set, clients should hide auto-generated link previews on the message for that user. Like other flags, it appears in the message's `flags` array and in `update_message_flags` events. The flag can be set on any message, whether or not it currently has a link preview.

## new feature level: 513

*2026-10-07 to 2026-10-07 · 2 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/412-api-documentation/topic/new.20feature.20level.3A.20513/with/2534813)*

**GitHub Actions** · 2026-10-07 09:18 UTC

#40322 has updated the API documentation for the following endpoints: 

* [`POST /messages/render`](/api/render-message): Added the `populate_url_embed_data` parameter, which requests that the server populate URL embed data for the content's links: data it already has is included in the rendered content, and the rest is fetched asynchronously and delivered via the new `url_embed_data` event.
* [`GET /events`](/api/get-events): Added a new `url_embed_data` event, sent to a user when the server has fetched URL embed data for content they asked it to render, so that a client displaying the rendered content can live-update it.

**Chris Bobbe** · 2026-10-07 17:38 UTC

No mobile issue needed; we'll naturally consider this feature when implementing #F178, "Previews when composing a message".
